name: Approve investments at the investment committee
summary: Direct investments, co-investments, fund commitments, new external mandates, follow-ons and exits above an asset class team's authority go to the weekly Management Investment Committee, co-chaired by the chief investment officer and chief risk officer with the general counsel. The investment office checks the approval level, collects the sponsor's sign-off, the independent risk opinion and a compliance check, circulates the pack, records the decision and any conditions, and sends items above the committee's authority to the board's investment committee. Elapsed time is driven by the weekly cut-off, members' calendars, risk review queues and, for large items, the board calendar, which presses deal teams facing seller deadlines.

baseline.org_archetype: A provincial not-for-profit asset manager of about 240 staff that invests about $79 billion for a few public pension plans and an insurance board through pooled funds and segregated accounts, on a cost recovery basis.
baseline.notes: Investment Department Committees for total portfolio, equities and credit and real assets were set up in 2021 to approve smaller items; a Board Investment Committee of all directors was created in September 2021. The memo and the risk opinion are produced in upstream processes and enter here ready for review.

trigger: A deal team, manager research or a private markets team submits an investment memo with its independent risk opinion and asks for a committee decision.
end_state: The decision and any conditions are recorded and communicated, conditions are confirmed met, or the item is rejected or rerouted; for items above the committee's authority, the board has decided.

volume.seasonality: More items before year end and before general partners' final closes; fewer in August.

steps.name: Book the submission on the committee agenda
steps.description: A deal team asks the investment office for a slot at an upcoming weekly committee meeting. The office logs the item in the pipeline tracker with its type (direct investment, co-investment, fund commitment, new mandate, follow-on or exit), size, stage (preliminary or final approval) and any seller or closing deadline.

error.defect_description: Deal size or type is logged wrongly.

evidence.note: About 35 direct and co-investment transactions in 2021 plus commitments, mandates and exits; staged committee practice. Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Check the approval level and required sign-offs
steps.description: The investment office compares the size and type of the item with the delegated approval authorities: below a threshold it goes to the relevant Investment Department Committee, otherwise to the Management Investment Committee, and above that committee's authority to the board. It lists the sign-offs the paper needs: risk opinion, legal and compliance.

error.defect_description: An item is routed to a body without enough authority.

control.basis: The model manager Investment Approval Policy and delegated authorities between the board, Management Investment Committee and Investment Department Committees

evidence.note: Delegation to Investment Department Committees up to thresholds and board approval of material investments are stated; reroute share is an author estimate.

steps.name: Sponsoring head signs off the memo
steps.description: The asset class head reviews the investment memo, the model, the sizing and the split across client accounts or pools, and signs it off for submission or sends it back to the deal team for more work.

error.defect_description: A weak assumption in the model is not challenged.

next.condition: preliminary or novel item for CIO pre-screen
returned to the deal team and reviewed again

evidence.note: Author estimate of common practice.

steps.name: CIO pre-screens the item
steps.description: For preliminary approvals and new strategies, the chief investment officer previews the memo outline at the weekly pipeline meeting and decides whether it is ready for the committee or needs more work first.

evidence.note: Tiered pre-committee reviews are common in private investing; share and times are author estimates.

steps.name: Sign off the independent risk opinion
steps.description: The director of investment risk oversight reviews the written risk opinion prepared by the risk team on the final memo (concentration, leverage, liquidity, currency, fit with risk budgets) and signs it for the committee pack; preliminary items get a short risk note. Risk questions sometimes force memo changes.

control.basis: Independent risk review of new investments before a committee decision (risk function separate from investment teams)

evidence.note: Independent risk reviews of transactions and separate risk control are described; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Check compliance, conflicts and allocation
steps.description: A compliance analyst checks the restricted list and staff conflicts, whether regulatory filings are needed (ownership, competition or foreign investment), and that the split of the investment across client accounts and pools follows each client's restrictions and the allocation policy.

error.defect_description: A needed filing or a client restriction is missed.

control.basis: OSC exemption order on the model manager: compliance system prevents contraventions of each investment management agreement and allocates opportunities fairly among members and pools

evidence.note: The order requires fairness in allocation and prevention of contraventions; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Assemble and circulate the committee pack
steps.description: The investment office checks the paper against the committee template, adds the risk opinion, compliance note and draft resolution, places it on the agenda and circulates the pack to members before the weekly cut-off. Papers that miss the cut-off wait a week.

error.defect_description: An outdated memo version is circulated.

control.basis: Committee mandate: papers circulated to members before the meeting

evidence.note: Members need materials in advance to prepare; weekly cut-off is an author estimate.

steps.name: Members read the pack and send questions
steps.description: Committee members, including the chief risk officer and general counsel, read the pack and send questions to the deal team through the investment office.

evidence.note: Author estimate; only one member's reading time is counted.

steps.name: Deal team answers pre-read questions
steps.description: The deal team prepares short written answers or extra analysis, such as a downside case or a different client split, and the investment office adds them to the pack.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Committee hears the deal team and decides
steps.description: The Management Investment Committee, co-chaired by the chief investment officer and chief risk officer with the general counsel and other senior managers, hears the deal team, questions the case, records recusals and approves, approves with conditions, recommends the item to the board, defers it for more work or rejects it.

control.basis: Management Investment Committee mandate: approval, review and governance process for investment decisions; every decision needing board approval is first recommended by the committee

evidence.note: Committee composition and its recommending role are stated; decision shares and times are author estimates.

steps.name: Record the decision and conditions
steps.description: The investment office writes the decision record: the approval, any conditions, the amount by client account or pool, recusals and the vote, and logs it in the approvals register against delegated limits for quarterly reporting to the board.

error.defect_description: A condition is recorded differently from what was decided.

evidence.note: Votes and recusals are recorded; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Co-chair confirms the decision record
steps.description: The chief investment officer, as co-chair, reads the draft decision record, corrects the wording of any conditions or amounts by client account, and confirms it as the official record.

control.basis: Decision records confirmed by the committee chair

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Communicate the decision
steps.description: The investment office emails the decision memo to the deal team, legal, private markets operations and finance so the team can sign or bid, legal can start documents and operations can prepare funding.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Deal team evidences the conditions
steps.description: Where approval carried conditions, such as a maximum price, final terms, a confirmatory diligence finding or a co-investor's commitment, the deal team gathers the evidence as the deal progresses and sends it to the investment office.

error.defect_description: Evidence is incomplete for one condition.

evidence.note: Approvals are tied to valuation ranges and budgets; confirmatory diligence takes three to six weeks.

steps.name: Confirm the conditions are met
steps.description: The director of investment risk oversight, with the investment office, checks the evidence against each condition and closes the item in the register, or sends it back to the committee if a condition cannot be met.

control.basis: Conditions of approval verified before closing

next.condition: condition not met, back to committee

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Rework the memo after deferral
steps.description: The deal team does the extra work the committee asked for, such as more diligence, a revised price or a smaller commitment, and resubmits for a later meeting.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Prepare the board recommendation paper
steps.description: For items above the committee's authority, the investment office turns the memo, risk opinion and committee recommendation into a board paper with a draft resolution for the Board Investment Committee (from September 2021) or the board.

evidence.note: The Board Investment Committee approves investment decisions above management authority; times are author estimates.

steps.name: CEO reviews and recommends to the board
steps.description: The chief executive reviews the board paper and the committee's recommendation and signs the recommendation, sometimes after a call with the deal team.

control.basis: Investment Approval Policy: material investment decisions approved by the board

evidence.note: Board approval of material investment decisions is stated; the CEO's review is an author assumption.

steps.name: Board investment committee decides
steps.description: The Board Investment Committee, made up of all directors, considers the item at its next meeting or at a special meeting called for a seller deadline, and approves, defers or rejects it.

control.basis: Board Investment Committee mandate: review and approve investment decisions and activities

evidence.note: The committee met twice in late 2021 and seven times in 2022; outcome shares and waits are author estimates.

steps.name: Record the rejection and notify the deal team
steps.description: The investment office records the rejection and its reasons in the register and tells the deal team, which informs the seller or general partner.

evidence.note: Most opportunities reviewed by investment committees do not close; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Record the board decision and communicate
steps.description: The investment office records the board resolution with any conditions in the approvals register and sends the decision to the deal team, legal and operations so documents and funding can proceed.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

exceptions.name: Item within department committee authority
exceptions.description: The size or type is within an Investment Department Committee's threshold, so the item leaves this process.

exceptions.name: Memo returned before submission
exceptions.description: The sponsoring head, the CIO's pre-screen or risk questions send the memo back to the deal team.

exceptions.name: Deferred for more work
exceptions.description: The committee asks for more diligence, a different price or a smaller size and the item returns to a later meeting.

exceptions.name: Board approval needed
exceptions.description: The item is above the committee's authority and goes to the Board Investment Committee, often at a special meeting when a seller deadline is close.

exceptions.name: Conditions precedent
exceptions.description: Approval carries conditions that the deal team must evidence before signing; a condition that cannot be met returns the item to the committee.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from booking on the agenda to the decision being communicated (or conditions closed)
benchmarks.population: Management Investment Committee submissions at a Canadian public-sector asset manager

evidence.note: Author estimate: one to three weekly cycles for a typical item; board items and conditions add several weeks.

benchmarks.population: The model manager Board Investment Committee (created 23 September 2021)

evidence.note: Stated in the 2021 and 2022 annual reports.
Stated in the 2021 results release.

benchmarks.unit: about 6 closed per 62 reviewed by the committee
benchmarks.population: Private equity investors surveyed by Gompers, Kaplan and Mukharlyamov

evidence.note: Deal funnel figures from the survey; buyout firms rather than asset owners.

pain_points.description: Papers that miss the weekly cut-off or wait for a risk opinion lose a week, which presses deal teams facing seller deadlines.

evidence.note: Author judgement from the step structure; the organisation file notes committee dates set the pace for deal teams.

pain_points.description: Several reviews before the meeting (sponsor, CIO pre-screen, risk, compliance) each can send the memo back.

evidence.note: Tiered approval processes add gates and documentation at each stage.

pain_points.description: Items above management authority wait for the board's investment committee, which met only twice in late 2021 and seven times in 2022, so special meetings are needed for deadlines.

evidence.note: Meeting counts are stated.

assumptions: The organisation file describes the committee as chaired by the CIO with the CEO and chief risk officer; the model manager's 2021 and 2022 annual reports describe it as co-chaired by the CIO and chief risk officer with the general counsel and other senior managers. This workflow follows the annual reports and has the CEO review only items going to the board.

Deal-team steps are shown under md_private_equity as the representative sponsor; the infrastructure, real estate and credit heads do the same steps with the same cost range. compliance_analyst is an organisation file role added for the compliance check.
Only one member's reading time (the chief risk officer's) is counted at s08; other members' reading and meeting time is not counted as hands-on time.
The share of items above the committee's authority (10%), deferrals (8%), rejections (4%) and conditional approvals (30%) are author estimates; the model manager has not published its thresholds.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's ranges.

sources.title: Endowment Governance Part 3: Process and Engagement
sources.supports: Chair owns the agenda with staff; materials at least a week before the meeting; regular meetings of two to four hours; record attendance, votes by name and recusals; circulate minutes promptly to confirm decisions; members should vote on asset allocation, benchmark and risk parameter changes.

sources.title: Investment-Decision Process (Twenty-four ways to classify private equity firms)
sources.supports: Decision processes range from a single central committee meeting twice a week to tiered pre-IC, interim and final committees and cheque-size limits below which heads approve alone.

sources.title: Private Equity New Investment Process
sources.supports: Staged committee approvals: short first review, 30 to 40 page preliminary memo, final memo with a recommended price; approvals tied to valuation ranges and budgets; confirmatory diligence takes three to six weeks.

sources.title: What Do Private Equity Firms Say They Do? (NBER Working Paper 21133)
sources.supports: Survey deal funnel: of 100 opportunities about 62 are reviewed with the partner group or investment committee, 24 get deep diligence, 14 reach a signed agreement and 6 close. Read from a text copy saved under scratch/.
